archetype.name: Gunslinger (boxed into a run-first plan)
archetype.definition: A quarterback who has always lived on aggressive throws downfield and over the middle, now asked to be the low-volume complement to a top-three defense and a run-leaning offense, and absorbing too many sacks while he waits for the big play.

report.headline: The sacks and the one-score collapses, not the arm, are sinking Mayfield's season
report.take:
Mayfield's profile hasn't changed much at its core. He still holds the ball, still hunts the throw past the sticks, and still takes sacks rather than throw it away. His pressure-to-sack rate has sat in the high 30s to mid 40s every year since 2021. What has changed is the setting. Tampa passes less than almost anyone relative to the situation (-7.5 pass rate over expected, 30th), the defense ranks 3rd in EPA, and Mayfield missed Weeks 4-6 with Jalon Daniels starting. He is averaging 158.4 passing yards a game, 58.8 fewer than last season, and his -0.151 EPA per dropback ranks 41st of 55.

The passing itself splits in two. When he pushes the ball, it works: throws of 10+ air yards are worth +0.165 a play with a 39.3% completion rate, deep balls +0.274, and the middle of the field +0.365. That is the 2023-24 version of him showing up in flashes. Everything underneath is a drain. Passes behind the line and in the 0-9 range are both negative, and the screen-and-checkdown game to Cade Otton (-0.191 per target) and Bucky Irving gives back what the shots earn.

The number that explains the season is the game-state split. Trailing by 9+, he is a good quarterback: +0.202 per play and a 4.1 CPOE. Within one score he is -0.413 per play, with 17 of his 22 sacks and almost all of his negative EPA. Third down tells the same story: -0.277 per play, 10 sacks, an average of 8.5 yards to go. In tight games defenses can sit on Tampa's long-yardage downs, and Mayfield's habit of extending into sacks turns punts into drives that go backward. The 11.2% sack rate (46th) and 45% pressure-to-sack rate (44th of 45) are the real story. The turnover line is partly noise: all three lost fumbles came in Week 1.

Where it goes from here: the arm talent is still visible in the downfield splits, and the one-score collapse is too extreme to hold at this level. But the volume ceiling is structural. A run-first plan backed by a top defense will keep his attempts in the mid-20s, so even a bounce-back looks like efficient 180-200-yard games rather than a return to 2024.

strengths.title: Downfield and middle throws still pay
strengths.body: His 10+ air-yard throws and middle-of-the-field attempts are clearly positive despite low completion rates. That is the classic gunslinger trade: misses, but explosive gains when it hits. He has done this across his career, and Chris Godwin Jr. (+0.251 per target) is the most productive outlet for it. On only 61 tenPlus attempts the exact rate is soft, but the shape matches who he has been.

strengths.title: Functional when the game opens up
strengths.body: Trailing by 9+, he has been efficient and accurate: +0.202 EPA per play and a 4.1 CPOE. Part of that is softer coverage in catch-up mode. It still shows the reads and throws are intact when he isn't working off third-and-long against a defense that knows a run is coming.

strengths.title: Scrambles still move chains
strengths.body: His scrambles return positive EPA and five first downs, and he ranks 18th in QB rushing yards. That is a real secondary weapon. It is also the flip side of his sack habit: the same holding of the ball that produces sacks produces these.

concerns.title: Sacks are wrecking drives
concerns.body: An 11.2% sack rate and a 45% pressure-to-sack rate rank near the bottom of the league, even though he is pressured at only a middling rate. He has always taken sacks (39.1% pressure-to-sack last season), so this is his trait amplified, not a new flaw. The scrambles don't come close to paying for it, and seven turnover-worthy fumbles show the ball-security cost.

concerns.title: One-score games and third downs
concerns.body: Within one score he is -0.413 EPA per play, with 17 sacks and a -7.5 CPOE. Third down is -0.277 at 8.5 yards to go. Long-yardage situations created by a run-first plan let defenses pin their ears back. Some regression toward average is likely at this extreme, but the setup won't change.

concerns.title: Low-volume role caps the ceiling
concerns.body: Tampa ranks 30th in pass rate over expected, and blowout wins produced 11- and 3-attempt games. With a top-three defense creating comfortable scripts, he will rarely be asked to throw 35 times. That role suppresses yardage regardless of how well he plays.

trend.note: His passing EPA has swung from game to game: deep negatives against Cleveland, Minnesota and Chicago, positive outings at Carolina and Detroit. Week 11 in Detroit (+5.5, two TDs) was his best game, but it came against the 27th-ranked defense, and his last-three CPOE of -5.3 says accuracy hasn't come back yet.

nextGame.headline: Carolina's missing pass rush is exactly what his sack problem needs
nextGame.body:
Carolina ranks last in hit rate and 31st in sack rate, which goes straight at Mayfield's biggest problem. If he isn't getting home-run sacked on third down, his drive-killing one-score numbers should improve. The Panthers are 21st against the pass overall but 2nd at limiting explosive passes, so the shot plays that fuel his EPA may be harder to hit. The likelier path is a steady, sack-free game. Tampa is a 3-point home favorite with a 43.5 total. In the Week 7 meeting they won 43-13 and he threw only 11 passes, so a lopsided script could again cap his volume.

Availability: Mayfield carried a Questionable tag with limited practice into Week 11 and still played every snap, so watch this week's report, but nothing points to him missing time. On Carolina's side, corner Jaycee Horn is on IR with an estimated return of December 6, and linebacker Bobby Okereke (89% of snaps) is out. Losing Okereke thins the coverage underneath and over the middle, where Mayfield is most efficient and where Otton works.

keyMatchups.title: Mayfield's sack habit vs no rush
keyMatchups.body: Carolina is last in hit rate and 31st in sack rate. Clean pockets give him time to let deep and middle routes develop without his tendency to hold the ball turning into sacks. This is the single biggest edge in the game.

keyMatchups.title: Tight end over the middle
keyMatchups.body: Carolina ranks 26th in EPA allowed to top tight ends and 27th against their averages, and Okereke is out. Otton has been a drag on Mayfield's season (-0.191 per target), but this is the matchup where those middle throws should play.

keyMatchups.title: Explosives are harder here
keyMatchups.body: Carolina is 2nd in limiting explosive passes and 4th in EPA allowed to WR1s, which bears on Emeka Egbuka. Mayfield's deep shots, his best-producing throws, may have to give way to a more methodical game.

nextGame.watch: His third-down sack count. If Carolina's rush can't get home, his one-score drives finally have a chance to finish.

restOfSeason.body:
Expect improvement in efficiency more than in volume. The one-score and third-down collapse is extreme enough that some regression toward his normal level is likely, especially against weaker pass rushes. The early fumble pile-up was a single-game event. The downfield game has stayed productive throughout, which says the arm is fine. What isn't going away is the structure: a run-leaning offense and a top-three defense keep his attempts in the low-to-mid 20s, and his sack tendency is a career-long trait that will keep showing up against good fronts.

That points to roughly 165-215 passing yards a game and somewhere between 0.8 and 1.4 touchdown passes, with scrambles adding 12-24 rushing yards. Sacks should settle somewhat but remain above league average, around 2 to 3.5 a game. A return to 2024 form would require a game script Tampa's defense rarely creates.
swingFactors: Whether his sack rate drops against weaker pass rushes
Game scripts created by Tampa's top-three defense
His health after a limited practice week

confidence.note: Seven games including two near-zero-volume outings and a three-week absence; core traits match his career.
